text:
ConocoPhillips edged up 0.64% today after falling steadily for a week, as oil prices stabilized. US crude held at $83.90 per barrel after dropping sharply in recent days—the stock had slid roughly 4% from August 21st through yesterday as crude declined. The slight recovery today reflects a modest steadying in the oil market rather than new company-specific news.

The broader context is geopolitical tension around Iran and the Strait of Hormuz, a critical chokepoint for global oil supply. The U.S. has escalated economic sanctions on Iran's banking and oil sectors, which theoretically could tighten oil supply and support prices—but so far the week's price action suggests traders are skeptical that these measures will meaningfully disrupt flows, or are more focused on recession concerns outweighing supply-side support.
